notes.title: Train World Update — Coupling & Uncoupling Arrives!
notes.content:
A major new gameplay feature is here: manual wagon coupling and uncoupling! This update brings deeper control, new waypoint tools, new locomotives, and dozens of improvements and fixes.
[h2]🔩 New Features & Mechanics[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]Coupling and Uncoupling of Wagons[/b] - trains can now uncouple and re-couple wagons at designated waypoints. Coupling is only possible with wagons that were previously uncoupled. Includes new sounds, a tutorial, and error handling for uncoupled locomotives.
[*] [b]Trains Without Wagons or Locomotives Remain on Tracks[/b] - wagons without locomotives stay on the  rails, and locomotive-only trains can move independently
[*] [b]Movement in Reverse[/b] - available at waypoints where a train changes direction (signals and passenger stations). Enables more advanced route setups.
[*] [b]Coupling & Uncoupling Tutorial[/b] - a step-by-step guide that walks players through how to manage this new mechanic.
[/list]
[h2]🚦 Waypoint System Updates[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]Priority Load[/b] - when enabled, a train will prioritize loading cargo/passengers specifically for the selected connection.
[*] [b]Wait for Full Train[/b] - train waits until fully loaded (based on selected percentage or amount) with any available cargo/passengers.
[*] [b]Waypoint UI[/b] - updated Waypoint Settings Interface and new icons for active options like “Full train”. Now waypoint settings can be edited without entering route edit mode
[/list]
[h2]🚆 New Locomotives[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]0-8-0 USRA[/b] (2nd Era Steam)
[*] [b]SDP40F[/b] (3rd Era Diesel)
[/list]
[h2]⚙️ Gameplay Improvements[/h2]
[list]
[*] Updated steam engine stats (power, speed, and price now reflect historical data)
[*] Adjusted one-time contract cargo amounts and rewards
[*] Population growth tuning (affects production)
[*] Adjusted production rates for Aluminum and Machines industries
[*] Optimized CPU and memory usage in train simulation
[*] Large train list display performance significantly improved
[*] Added UI scaling setting
[/list]
[h2]🎨 Visual & UI Updates[/h2]
[list]
[*] Updated loading screen backgrounds
[*] Updated brick tunnel entrance model
[*] Fixed missing shadows in cities
[*] Adjusted shadow distance parameters
[*] Updated general UI style
[*] Time labels added to “Full Load” and “Wait for Connection”
[*] Labels added to the age graph in "Replace" and "Inventory" panels
[/list]
[h2]🧰 Fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Resolved issue with trains getting stuck at stations with specific waypoint configurations
[*] Fixed “Mastering the Research Tree” tutorial
[*] Resolved game hang on failed save file load
[*] Fixed train stopping abruptly at signals
[*] Train jumping when editing active routes
[*] Trains no longer stop on signal waypoints when load conditions are already met
[*] Incorrect cargo/passenger display after removing trains
[*] Fixed long locomotives hanging off rails
[*] Fixed display issues with stations, depots, signals, and contract connections
[*] Corrected one-time contract cargo amount display
[*] Resolved incorrect wait time calculations for full train/connection options
[*] Max wait time for auto-wait and full load set to 90 minutes
[*] Resolved flipped values in the “Targets and Statistics” panel
[*] Fixed game freezing on save files with corrupted rails
[*] Train display and payments are now correctly handled
[*] Fixed UI waypoint button error
[*] Fixed freight priority logic
[*] Fixed rail placement for locomotives
[*] Trains now properly resume movement after signal wait with fulfilled load condition
[*] Various language fixes
[/list]
🛤️ This first implementation of wagon coupling/uncoupling lays the foundation for more interesting features. Stay tuned for future updates!

💬 Let me know how you’re using coupling in your networks!
Your feedback drives development — join the conversation and share your creations.

notes.title: New Features & Steam Locomotives!
notes.content:
[h2]Hello, Railway Managers![/h2]
The past few weeks have been packed with updates, and I am excited to bring you a massive list of improvements, optimizations, and new features for Train World! From quality-of-life upgrades to brand-new locomotives, there's a lot to cover—so let's dive in.
[h3]🚂 New Steam Locomotives[/h3]
[list]
[*] 0-6-0 Portola (Era 1)
[*] 2-10-4 Texas (Era 2)
[*] 2-8-4 Berkshire (Era 2)
[*] 4-6-2 Pacific (Era 1)
[/list][h3]📊 Industries & Production Panel[/h3]
[list]
[*] New UI to track all available industries across your unlocked regions
[*] View available production chains and plan your industry expansions with ease
[/list][h3]🛠 Major Optimizations & Fixes[/h3]
[list]
[*] New "Sell excess wagons" toggle in the Replace panel—excess wagons are automatically sold if the new train setup doesn't match length requirements
[*] Updated train panels with larger Replace and Inventory sections
[*] "Remove all" button added to quickly clear train layouts
[*] Improved route visualization—now you can track the current train's route in Follow Camera mode
[*] Pathfinding Optimizations—significantly reduced memory usage and improved performance, especially with large train networks (50+ trains)
[*] Fixed multiple issues, including saved game loading errors, passenger display issues, and waypoint auto-wait errors
[/list][h3]🎛 Enhanced User Controls & Customization[/h3]
[list]
[*] New train pause mechanic—trains can now be stopped at waypoints without requiring a route edit
[*] Updated train panels—Replace and Waypoint panels are now more user-friendly, plus you can now select multiple save files for deletion
[*] New "Auto-renew on low lifespan" toggle—when enabled, trains with low lifespan will auto-renew if possible
[/list][h3]🌍 Enhanced Visuals & Immersion[/h3]
[list]
[*] Updated terrain modifications for bridges, tunnels, and tracks, fixing grass patches and terrain edges
[*] Stylized background images added to the loading screen for a fresh new look
[*] Updated biomes & improved animal placement for better visual realism
[*] Updated rail color coding in Map View & Minimap for better clarity
[*] Inside train sound effects! Experience the rush of being onboard with realistic train horns (H key) and new follow-camera wind sounds
[/list][h3]🔧 QoL Upgrades & Bug Fixes[/h3]
[list]
[*] New graphics settings: Toggle sun movement and cloud shadows
[*] New alphabetical sorting for the Connections list
[*] Waypoint UI improvements—Updated Remove button position to reduce misclicks
[*] Fixed missing passengers—Passengers now appear correctly on stations even after reloading a save
[*] Fixed various errors with routes, train lists, waypoints, localization, and UI interactions
[*] These updates are all designed to improve your gameplay experience, whether it's optimizing train performance, enhancing visuals, or making management easier. We’re continuing to refine Train World based on your feedback, so keep those suggestions coming!
[/list][h3]🚆 What’s next?[/h3]
I am already working on new gameplay mechanics, locomotives, and optimizations that will further enhance your railway empire. Stay tuned for more updates, and don’t forget to share your thoughts!

See you on the rail tracks! 🚆🔥

notes.title: 🚂 Silverstream Update & More! 🌟
notes.content:
[h2]Hello, Train World community![/h2]
I’m thrilled to share some exciting updates and improvements we’ve made recently. These changes are designed to enhance your gameplay experience and add new depth to the world of Train World. Let’s dive into what’s new!
[h3]🌍New Content:[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Silverstream Bay Map:[/b] Explore this charming new map featuring a central shipping lane, picturesque mountain ranges, and a flowing river.
[/list][h3]🛠️Gameplay Enhancements:[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Wagons Panel:[/b] Easily view available cargo types and compatible wagons with the new Wagons panel, accessible next to the "Help" button.
[*] [b]Prestige Mechanic: [/b]Keep track of your Prestige, which grows through activities like purchasing trains, unlocking regions, and more. Prestige decay ensures active gameplay, adding a new layer of strategy.
[/list][h3]🎯 Map Targets and Achievements:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Complete map targets with achievements to "win" the map and earn stars based on the difficulty level.
[/list][h3]🌅 Visual & UI Improvements:[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Dynamic Daylight: [/b]Enjoy beautiful daylight color changes based on the sun’s angle.
[*] [b]Enhanced Minimap: [/b]Navigate with ease thanks to color-coded rails, optimized icon sizes, and new icons for village production.
[/list][h3]⚖️ Balancing Adjustments:[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Loans & Region Prices:[/b] I’ve fine-tuned loan rates and region prices, with adjustments based on the number of regions you have unlocked.
[/list][h3]🐞 Bug Fixes:[/h3]
[list]
[*] I’ve squashed several bugs, including terrain holes, UI layout issues, and tooltip glitches. Plus, improvements to signal placement and locomotive replacement ensure smoother gameplay.
[/list][h3]⚙️ Engine Update:[/h3]
[list]
[*] I’ve upgraded to Unity 6 LTS for better performance and to prepare for future enhancements.
[/list]
[h2]🗣️ Your Feedback Matters[/h2]
Your feedback is invaluable to me! I’m committed to listening to your suggestions and improving Train World based on what you share. Please keep the feedback coming—I’m always looking for ways to make the game better for you.
[h2]🚆 Coming Soon: Train World Driver Beta[/h2]
I’m also excited to announce that the Train World Driver Beta is just around the corner! Stay tuned for more information on how you can get involved and experience the next evolution of Train World.

Thank you for your continued support and passion for Train World. Let’s keep building something amazing together!

Happy railroading!

I'm thrilled to share the latest round of updates for Train World! These changes focus on making your experience even smoother, more visually appealing, and customizable. Here's what you can expect in these latest updates:

[*]Added a variety of new camera views for following trains, perfect for watching your locomotives from fresh angles.
[*]Updated the camera-follow UI, along with convenient key bindings for switching views.

[*]Adjusted render distance settings to control max camera height and improve performance for lower-spec systems. [/list]
[h2]🚉 New & Updated Locomotives[/h2] [list]

[*]New Arrivals: Third-era diesel locomotives FM H-24-66, C 30-7, and second-era GP 7!

[*]Graphs in the economy panel have been upgraded for better clarity, along with improved filter behavior.
[*]New line charts in the economy panel, replacing bar charts for select stats. [/list]
[h2]🌿 Immersive Environment Updates[/h2] [list]

notes.title: Double Specializations, New Locomotives, and More!
notes.content:
Dear Engineers,

I’m excited to share a series of updates to Train World that bring fresh features, improvements, and significant gameplay enhancements. These updates will have a major impact on your rail empire, particularly with the new economic dynamics. 

[h2]Major Economy Update: Double Specialization Per Region[/h2]
One of the most impactful changes is the [b]new double specialization feature[/b] for regions, revolutionizing how you manage your economy:
[list] 
[*] [b]Each region now supports two specializations[/b], providing greater production diversity and more complex logistics challenges. 
[*] [b]Cities can now host two production facilities[/b], doubling their output potential and offering new strategies for resource management. 
[*] Maps have been updated to reflect these changes, and I’ve improved the UI to make it easier to manage the expanded economy system. 
[/list]
This update drastically enhances gameplay by giving you more control over your production chains, unlocking deeper strategic planning as you expand your rail empire.

[h2]New Locomotives & Train Management Improvements[/h2]
First, let’s talk about the new locomotives:
[list] 
[*] First-Era Steam Locomotives: The [b]0-4-4 T Onward[/b] and [b]2-6-6 T Mason[/b] are now available, adding new historical depth to your early rail networks. 
[*] Third-Era Diesel Locomotives: Modernize your railways with the powerful [b]F 40 PH[/b] and [b]SD 70ACe T4[/b]. 
[*] Locomotive parameters for the [b]Mogul[/b] and [b]PS 10[/b] have been updated to improve their overall performance and efficiency. 
[/list]
[h2]Improved Train Management Tools[/h2]
Several new features have been added to help you keep your trains running smoothly:
[list] 
[*] A new “[b]Lifespan is at the end[/b]” warning icon helps you keep your fleet in top shape. 
[*] [b]Utilization[/b] and [b]Wait Time[/b] sorting options have been added to the [b]Economy[/b] panel to help you locate inefficiencies quickly.
[*] [b]Train Filters & Layout[/b]: Train lists in the [b]Trains[/b] and [b]Economy[/b] panels now have expanded filtering options, allowing for faster and more detailed management. Plus, a new [b]Minimize/Maximize[/b] button has been added to streamline your interface. 
[/list]
[h2]New Tutorials & UI Enhancements[/h2]
Several new tutorial sections have been added to help players navigate complex game mechanics:
[list] 
[*] [b]Rail Types and Color-Coding[/b]: Learn more about how rail types affect your routes and how to interpret color-coding during construction. 
[*] [b]Fast Rail Construction[/b] and [b]Advanced Signal Operations[/b]: New sections provide detailed insights into optimizing your rail network. 
[*] [b]Waypoint Options and Route Optimizations[/b]: Improve the efficiency of your train routes with a deeper dive into waypoints and route planning. 
[/list]
The [b]Signals[/b] panel UI has also been updated, and I’ve added improvements to the [b]Construction UI[/b] for a smoother experience when planning and expanding your network.

[h2]Other Updates and Fixes[/h2]
Here are some additional improvements and bug fixes across various aspects of the game:
[list] 
[*] The [b]lumber cargo model[/b] for all platform wagons has been updated. 
[*] Fixed bugs related to signal tooltips, train jumping, and rail construction near junctions. 
[*] [b]Increased wagon limit[/b]: You can now have up to [b]250 wagons[/b] per train. 
[*] Numerous UI updates to the [b]Economy[/b] and [b]Information[/b] panels, including fixing data presentation and improving layout clarity. 
[/list]
I’m committed to continuing to improve Train World based on your feedback and ideas. This update is a significant step forward, and I hope these new features enhance your gameplay experience. Don’t forget to share your thoughts and experiences in the community forums!

Stay tuned for more exciting updates, and thank you for your continued support!

notes.content:
Hello, Train World Engineers!

I am excited to bring you the latest update, Version 1.17.50, packed with new content, improvements, and bug fixes. notes.title: Industry, ports, and more
notes.content:
Hi everyone!

I am happy to announce a new big update in Train World is live. Here are the changes that were made to the game since the last announcement.

[h3]New features[/h3]
[list]
[*] Added ability to set production in the cities. Now players will have to choose where each factory goes or what cargo the city is going to produce. There are multiple strategies possible as to how you assign production: shorter distances, higher train utilization, or maximum cargo consumption. Also, players will be able to see in advance what production will be available in the future and plan rail network expansion accordingly. Cities that have production in them will show industry buildings. 
[*] Access to ports is now available. A nearby city will turn into a port city and will start to generate contracts to and from it. Also, ports will provide access to resources needed for production that are not available on the map. Some old maps were updated with ports as well. Port models and ship models were added.
[/list]
[h3]New content[/h3]
[list]
[*] New locomotives were added as well: a unique-looking PS-10 based on a narrow-gauge Yosemite Mountain Sugar Pine Railroad train, EL 3A was one of the first Westinghouse electric locomotives, and the famous shark nose Baldwin RF16 comes in both A and AB variants. Also, SD 40 received a model update.
[*] Talquell Peak is a small map with a river in the middle. Regions are small but mountains and terraces require a bit of planning from the player. At the same time, they create some very scenic views. 
[*] Montara Cove is a medium size map that also packs a lot of beautiful locations. The port will be a central point in gameplay here as it can access every region. You will find all kinds of terrain here from almost flat planes to mountains and valleys. 
[/list]
[h3]Quality-of-life features and improvements[/h3]
[list]
[*] All pick panels and major UI options are saved to the save file. Now you will be able to continue playing with all the pick panels open and right from the spot that you left. 
[*] All major panels received a key shortcut. You can change those to your liking in the settings menu.
[*] New localizations were added in the past weeks as well. Brazilian Portuguese, Korean, Japanese, and Simplified Chinese became available in the game.
[/list]

[h3]Plans for the future[/h3]
[list]
[*] More locomotives and trains. Many trains were never represented in the games. We know very little about a lot of interesting, cool-looking, and unique trains, and I would like to change that. 
[*] More maps. I believe with each map my skills in map-making are getting better and better. 
[*] More features to interact with cities. Adding new buildings will have an impact on cargo consumption, passenger generation, etc.
[*] Balancing economy, reputation update, and continuous improvements. Some tasks are just always there. 
[/list]

A lot of bug fixes, improvements, and smaller changes were done during the past month. You can find a detailed description of all the changes in the Release Notes thread of the  Discussions section. More information can be found on Discord. As always, I am happy to answer all your questions in Discussions, Discord, or via e-mail. Thank you for your support and interest in the project!

notes.title: Happy new year!
notes.content:
I wish you a Happy New Year! To be honest, this was not an easy year to put it lightly. Most important we made it. The release and first big update are behind us. A lot was achieved, mistakes were made, and a lot of knowledge and experience was picked up.

During the past week a lot of small updates and fixes were made. Here is an overview on what was done:
[list]
[*] Fixed train teleportation on rail/signal construction
[*] Fixed train teleportation on train wagons edit
[*] Improved incorrect direction of movement on route edit
[*] Reduced prices on the passenger wagons for medium era
[*] Numerous localization fixes
[*] Added station name to station options panel
[*] Fixed a couple of small bugs
[*] Fixed stuck passengers after route edit
[*] Fixed terminal selection
[*] Fixed incorrect waypoint selection after route edit
[*] Reputation points for region opening is lowered a bit
[*] Fixed estimated train speed calculations for freight trains
[*] Fixed incorrect lifespan calculation in certain cases
[*] Updated braking, trains stop a bit faster now
[*] Fixed passenger trains skipping wait time on signals
[*] Fixed train edit issues (incorrect wagon amount calculation)
[*] Fixed set trains edit
[*] Added low power cap (trains with a low power-to-weight ratio will throw an error and will not move). The fix eliminates excessive route time calculations for underpowered trains which could cause the game to hang
[*] Route time calculator optimized to avoid long calculation times for slow trains

notes.title: Development update
notes.content:
Hi, I want to give an update on the development process for the upcoming big changes to the game. I want to give a high-level 
 overview of what is in the works and also what is planned to be added in the update. Note, that all of the things below are current state descriptions and are subject to change

Transport logic:
[list]
[*]Passengers and freight are constantly transported by other means. The train transport now competes with these other means. So, no more situations when the production is not operating because one of the components is not delivered
[/list]

Economy:
[list]
[*]Passengers are separated into two categories: local and regional. Local passengers want to travel to the neighboring cities. Regional passengers want to travel between neighboring capitals 
[*]The player is able to set a price level per connection. This influences the number of passengers generated by the connection. The relationship is not linear so it allows for various strategies in passenger transport
[*]Freight transport is also split into two categories: one-time contracts and recurring deliveries. One-time contracts pay a fixed sum of money for a specific cargo delivered to the neighboring capital. Recurring requires a constant flow of cargo from the source to the destination. Recurring deliveries are split into batches. A player is able to adjust batch sizes that will be transported
[*]Transportation profits were significantly reworked. Now profits are calculated from actual spending (maintenance and train cost) and a set margin 
[/list]

Maps and industries:
[list]
[*]Maps will be significantly updated, and regions will be changed. Expect city density closer to the one seen in the "Noran Island" map.  The number of cities per region is reduced to four including the capital. So "Noran Isand" will have five regions
[*]Each region will have industry specialization with production centered around that specialization
[*]Regions do not have default consumption. This was replaced by industry-centered deliveries and one-time contracts
[*]Production facilities appear on the map as the player progresses with the game and the type of facilities that appear is random and depends on available resources
[*]The plan is to have over twenty industry specializations with more than a hundred production facilities and cargo types
[/list]

Trains:
[list]
[*]Trains are split into passenger and freight. Passenger trains will never be able to become freight trains and vice versa
[*]Lines were removed, and now trains have routes that a set per train. While cloning a train a player has an option to include the route
[*]Depots were added. Now the train has to get to the route from the closest depo
[*]Routes can end at the depot. This way the route will not be looped (very useful for one-time contracts)
[*]Cargo types are grouped (liquid, bulk, etc.). Now wagons and stations transport specific groups
[*]Added locomotives lifespan. When the train reaches the end of its lifespan the power drops significantly to the point that the train stops.  Lifespan affects sell price
[*]Added adjustable maintenance. Higher maintenance will cost more, but expend lifespan of the locomotive
[*]A few wagons will be added
[/list]

UI:
[list]
[*]Will reflect all the changes as well as some minor updates and improvements
[/list]

I will provide information on other changes in the next announcements. I hope you will like the changes. 

Important, previous saves will not be compatible with the new version. I will try to keep the old version of the game available on a separate branch.

notes.content:
The new game update is live. Here is the list of changes:
- A lot of backend fixes
- A player now has the ability to remove stations and signals that are assigned to lines
- It is possible to delete or modify rails occupied by trains

- Lists panels are made resizable in height (trains list, lines list, etc.)

I will continue working on improving the quality of the game as well as polishing various aspects. Also, I am constantly going through the list of requests and checking which ones I can implement right away and the rest are integrated into the future development. 

The decision was made to disable the demo and focus on the game improvements and feature development. The demo will be disabled on August 20, 2023. It served its purpose and now the demo takes too much resources to update frequently. Also, having two versions of the game increases the chance of making a mistake.

Thank you for your interest in the project and see you around.
